name: Spa-Francorchamps
blurb: Through the Ardennes forest: Eau Rouge without the hurry.

texts: Spa first held a race in 1921 on public roads, a lap of nearly fifteen kilometres.
The Spa twenty-four hours, one of the oldest endurance races in the world, was first run in 1924.
Spa is famous for its weather: it can rain on one part of the track while another stays dry.
In 2021 heavy rain meant the Belgian Grand Prix was run for only a couple of laps behind the safety car. It went down as the shortest race in Formula One history.
In 2024 George Russell won here, then was disqualified because his car was a kilo and a half too light, handing the win to his teammate, Lewis Hamilton.
Eau Rouge is named for the stream at the bottom, red from iron in the water. The climb beyond it is Raidillon.
Drivers take Eau Rouge and Raidillon almost flat out, climbing steeply as the car is pressed into the road.
At seven kilometres, this is the longest lap on the Formula One calendar.
The circuit is named after the nearby town of Spa, whose mineral springs gave the word spa to the world.
Michael Schumacher won at Spa six times, more than any other driver.
